title: Open detail D10b · Red “Remove” in the Calendar and Schedule
subtitle: Found by the rulebook-rows review; for the new-students prompt and §7's wording. The Calendar's Remove (an event or a closure) and the Schedule's Remove (a time slot) are red, act at once and offer a 5-second Undo (v0.233, v0.234) — after that the item is gone: there is no Removed list to bring it back from. Item 7 made red mean “gone for good” and kept Withdraw plain because Restore brings the person back later. The rows' new §7 sentence (“never Withdraw or other reversible removals”) reads as if these three turn plain — the question is which way to word it. Red that isn't in question (it asks first, nothing comes back): deleting an event type, a planned schedule, a prospect. (Preview screenshots · PC size · fake data)

2. Schedule → Edit time slot: the same red Remove.

columns.note: Pictures 3–4 are drawn over the real dialogs (only the Remove button's colour); nothing in the app was changed. Side finding, not part of this question: Forms' builder “Delete field” is red, acts at once and has no Undo — rule 1.4 says something that can't be undone asks first; it goes to phase 3.

footer:
Your choice — one question: what does “gone for good” mean for these three Remove buttons?
A · Recommended: keep them red, and §7 says what “gone for good” means: there is nothing to bring it back from later — the 5-second Undo is a safety net, not a way back. Withdraw stays plain because Restore brings the person back. + nothing changes on screen; red keeps warning where something really disappears. − two kinds of undo to tell apart (5 seconds vs Restore).
B · Plain, because they can be undone (pictures 3–4). + the simplest rule: Undo means no red. − removing an event, a closure or a class time looks harmless, though after 5 seconds it is gone for good; the trash icon still says “delete”.
C · Red, and they ask first, like Delete permanently. + “red always asks first” everywhere. − an extra step on a common admin task; the instant Undo goes (changes v0.233 / v0.234).
